prior_issues.description: Update method sends an empty Healthcheck struct with only modified fields — the Cloudflare API may interpret zero-value fields (Interval=0, Timeout=0, Retries=0, Suspended=false) as intentional updates rather than 'unchanged'. This is a potential correctness issue depending on the API behavior, though the current implementation matches the pattern used in other services in this project.

Get method unconditionally wraps errors as notFound — not all API errors are 404s (could be auth failure, network error, rate limit). Other services in this project have the same pattern, so it's consistent but semantically imprecise.

Missing CheckRegions, HTTPConfig, and TCPConfig from cloudflare.Healthcheck — the Healthcheck struct omits fields that users may need for HTTP-specific checks (expected status codes, headers, method) and TCP config, and for selecting check regions. These are important for non-trivial healthcheck setups.

Get() wraps all API errors as notFound — a 403 or 500 from Cloudflare would be misclassified as R2NotFoundError. Other services in the project have the same pattern so this is consistent, but still semantically wrong.

Missing CheckRegions, HTTPConfig, and TCPConfig fields from cloudflare.Healthcheck — the Healthcheck struct omits these fields that exist in the upstream type, which means users cannot configure check regions or protocol-specific settings (HTTP headers, method, expected codes, follow redirects; TCP method). This limits the usefulness of the library for non-trivial healthcheck configurations.
Get() and Update()'s fetch-error path wrap all API errors as notFound — a 403 or 500 is misclassified. Consistent with other services in the project but semantically imprecise.
Missing CheckRegions, HTTPConfig, and TCPConfig fields from cloudflare.Healthcheck limits non-trivial healthcheck setups (HTTP-specific settings, TCP config, region selection).

CheckHTTP creates a new http.Client per call instead of reusing d.httpClient — the redirect-tracking closure is the reason, but it means timeout and transport settings from the constructor are partially wasted (timeout is re-applied, but any custom transport would not be)

CheckSSL uses tls.DialWithDialer which does not respect the ctx cancellation — context is accepted but only the timeout from d.timeout is honored; a long-running TLS handshake won't cancel on ctx.Done()

queryResolver silently swallows individual DNS lookup errors (LookupHost, LookupMX, LookupNS) — if LookupHost fails but MX succeeds, the error from LookupHost is lost entirely rather than being surfaced in a warnings field
NewDomainService receives nil for DNS and SSL services — if GetDetail internally calls methods on those without nil-checking, it will panic rather than return an error

Dead flags: --priority and --paused are registered on both create and update commands (cmd/firewall.go:141-142, 150-151) but never passed to the library. Users who set these flags get silent data loss — the values are ignored with no warning.

Update does not pass existing filter ID to Cloudflare API (pkg/r2go2/firewall.go:148-150). The Filter in FirewallRuleUpdateParams has no ID field set, which may cause the CF API to create a duplicate filter instead of updating the existing one. This depends on CF API behavior but is a correctness risk.
